failure_summary.description: Agents selected metadata, a cited work, an etymon, or a related entity despite existing rules that identify the clue’s actual target.
Answers were close but included incidental modifiers or failed to match the conventional minimal answer form.
The fragment-completion guidance could encourage returning only a missing title component when the clue asks for the work itself.
A visual-reference clue was answered from a salient brand association rather than evidence identifying the depicted item.

patch.reasoning: Several errors already contradict explicit skill rules, so repeating those rules would not patch a gap. Clarify the ambiguity between completing a title fragment and identifying a whole work, make direct-definition answer forms more explicit, and add a narrow safeguard for visual-reference clues.

edits.target: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer the omitted word or phrase that completes the clue rather than echoing the supplied text.
edits.content: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer omitted wording when the clue explicitly asks for a completion. If the clue instead asks to identify a work or its title while giving only part of the title, return the full conventional title, not just the omitted word or supplied fragment.

edits.target: For direct definition or trivia clues, treat the description as a fill-in target and return the conventional term or category called for by the whole clue, including after elliptical wording such as “one of these.” Do not answer with a named example when the clue asks for its class, or repeat an embedded synonym that serves only as a cue rather than the target.
edits.content: For direct definition or trivia clues, treat the description as a fill-in target and return the conventional term or category called for by the whole clue, including after elliptical wording such as “one of these.” Do not answer with a named example when the clue asks for its class, or repeat an embedded synonym that serves only as a cue rather than the target. For common-noun answers, omit incidental brand, purpose, or other descriptive modifiers from the clue or context; retain an article only when it belongs in the conventional answer form.

For clues referring to an item “seen here” or otherwise relying on a depiction, identify the depicted item from visual evidence when available; do not substitute a familiar product merely because it is salient in the surrounding text. If the depiction is unavailable and the text supports multiple candidates, do not treat one as established without distinguishing evidence.
